The port methods do not themselves create the exclusive .sotp-rustdoc subtree or enumerate every possible rustdoc writer. capture_current delegates that ownership and lock participation to RustdocSchemaExporter and RustdocOutputLock; bound tests cover 120-second timeout, contention, and lock-operation fail-closed without retry.

load_from_path hashes one immutable baseline byte vector and does not mix generations of a live export. capture_current has no rustdoc invocation of its own: it delegates to RustdocSchemaExporter::capture_rustdoc_snapshot, which acquires RustdocOutputLock before expected-path selection and holds it through read_bytes. The port surface has no unlocked re-read path.

RustdocCrateAdapter::capture_current contains no cargo rustdoc invocation. It calls RustdocSchemaExporter::capture_rustdoc_snapshot, which acquires RustdocOutputLock before expected-path selection and holds that lock through JSON-byte read_bytes. Bound tests cover lock-operation failure, contention timeout, generation replacement, and locked-byte snapshot construction. The adapter has no second path that rereads Cargo output without the lock.

This adapter returns a hashed rustdoc snapshot. It does not compute implementation or resolution fingerprints and does not persist type-signal results, so start/end fingerprint agreement before persist is not adapter-local behavior.

This adapter does not assemble TypeSignalsCacheKey fingerprints or compare them after capture. It cannot accept ABA by declaring fingerprints unchanged via path reread; those checks are not operations of load_from_path or capture_current.

The port-relevant slice of CO-04 is constructing a validated rustdoc execution identity (crate, features, profile, expected JSON path) and hashing captured bytes. It is not the D3 workspace-file walk that produces ImplementationFingerprint; that walk is not a method of RustdocCratePort.

The port-relevant slice of AC-08 on this Unix host is fail-closed rejection of a symlinked or unverifiable workspace/target root before export. Unsupported-platform handling is compiled only under cfg(not(unix)) in rustdoc_output_lock and is not an executable branch of capture_current here.

This evaluator requires exclusive .sotp-rustdoc target ownership on resolved execution identities and fail-closes when a shared Cargo target is supplied. It does not acquire the 120-second rustdoc output lock, serialize concurrent exporters, or route writers through RustdocOutputLock; those lock-participation mechanics are performed by RustdocSchemaExporter during capture_current, not by this orchestration function.

This exporter copies rustdoc JSON bytes under a target-directory lock. It does not assemble TypeSignalsCacheKey, walk hermetic workspace inputs, or decide type-signal reuse from implementation fingerprints.

CO-04's complete authoritative-input admission and cache-identity policy are not operations of rustdoc JSON export. This adapter neither fingerprints the Cargo/rustc/rustdoc environment set nor compares cache keys.
This exporter has no type-signal document cache, worktree cleanliness check, or reuse skip path. AC-04's complete reuse gate is not local behavior of export_rustdoc_json.

This exporter verifies the expected JSON path and copies bytes inside the exclusive-target lock, then returns those bytes. It does not recheck implementation/resolution fingerprints before a type-signal persist step, because it has no type-signal writer.

Lock-held byte copy and expected-path verification are this exporter's AC-06 slice. It cannot observe ABA of TypeSignalsCacheKey fingerprints or uncooperative writers after persist, because it does not persist type-signal results.
